turns.assessment: The outage is a simultaneous, network-wide optical failure, not an isolated svc268 client or ODU fault. All affected working paths share roadm.S01, and coincident AMP_INPUT_LOS/OCH_LOS alarms appear on multiple directions from S01. That pattern strongly identifies a hard WSS input-port failure at the common ROADM; an OTN switch or client-port failure would not produce the optical loss alarms.

proposals.rationale: roadm.S01 is the sole listed dependency common to every affected working path. A failed WSS input port blocks all channels arriving on that degree and explains the synchronous multi-service loss, OCH_LOS, and downstream amplifier input-loss alarms.
A switch-fabric failure at the common node could interrupt many ODUs, but it would generate ODU-layer failures rather than the observed optical channel and amplifier input loss.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

clarify.assessment: Choose index 1. The S12→S01, S13→S01, and S20→S01 ingress telemetry explicitly remained unchanged, while the S04→S01 preamplifier lacks unchanged input/output-power evidence (only pump current was unchanged). That isolates the failed S01 WSS ingress most strongly to the S04→S01 degree.
